raw_document.title: FutureProof Textiles Eurocluster: 1st Open Call round Supporting SMEs in the Textile Sector towards Digital and Green Transition
raw_document.description: Opportunity FutureProof Textiles Eurocluster: 1st Open Call round Supporting SMEs in the Textile Sector towards Digital and Green Transition DEADLINE: 18 September 2026 Open Call objective: Empowering 40 SMEs in the textile sector to successfully navigate the "twin transitions" of digital transformation and green sustainability. Support: Beyond the €50,000 grant, FutureProofTextiles offers extensive capacity-building and networking resources to help build a connected SME ecosystem: Tailored Training: An average of 40 hours per SME focusing on digital transformation, circular economy principles, and sustainable production. Dedicated Mentoring: Custom technical consulting and mentoring sessions for up to 6 selected SMEs based on specific needs. Open-Access Materials: Production of 100 hours of scalable training curricula and best-practice guides for the broader textile sector. Cross-Border Networking: Facilitation of international collaboration to foster an innovative textile ecosystem. Link to the online Application Portal : https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/FutureProofTextiles-1st-OpenCall Who can apply: Company size Applicants must fall under the category of SME, according to European Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC* Partnerships Clusters and intermediary organisations are not eligible even if they are SMEs. Each applicant should represent a single SME, not a consortia of multiple SMEs. Industry Applicants must be SMEs operating in the textile value chain. SMEs from complementary sectors (e.g., tech, machinery) are also eligible, provided their proposed innovation directly contributes to the textile value chain. Activities must align with a relevant NACE code (or national equivalent), such as: Textile manufacturing: C13.1, C13.2, C13.3, C13.9 Apparel manufacturing: C14.1, C14.3 Textile-based products and technical textiles: C15.12, C22.19 Textile recycling and circularity: C38 Digital and innovative solutions for the textile sector: J62, J63 Manufacture of machinery for textile, apparel and leather production:C 28.94 Location Only SMEs legally established in countries participating in the Single Market Programme (SMP) are eligible to apply. This includes EU Member States and any other country formally associated with the SMP. A full list of participating countries is published here: List of participating countries in the Single Market Programme (SMP) Language The applicant SME must have at least one staff member who speaks English and will be actively involved in the implementation process, handling all communication needs with the consortium. Submission Rules: Platform Proposal submitted online on the EU Survey Platform. Any other means will not be accepted. Application Form Language Proposals must be written in English. Submissions done in any other language will not be evaluated. Submission Limit Applicant SMEs may submit up to two proposals per Open Call round (one under Green Transition and one under Digital Innovations). Despite this, each SME is eligible to receive a maximum of one grant award across the entire program. Proposal Requirements The proposal must demonstrate a Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 5 or higher. Compliance & Ethics Applicants must confirm their full compliance with all rules, including absence of double funding, and conflict of interest, by reviewing and signing the mandatory forms included in the application: Funding eligibility and absence of conflict of interest declaration form SME and Eligibility declaration form Step by Step Guide Applicants may submit one proposal for a Green Transition project and one for a Digital Innovation project. Please note that a separate application must be submitted for each. Link to the online Application Portal : https://ec.europa.eu/eusurvey/runner/FutureProofTextiles-1st-OpenCall Step 1: Verify Eligibility Review the eligibility requirements thoroughly to ensure your organization and project qualify for funding. Step 2: Concept & Budgeting Check out “Exhaustive List of Eligible Activities and Eligible Costs” document. Check out “Needs of the SMEs in the Textile Sector” document, which helps the brainstorming process. Brainstorm your proposal. When brainstorming, keep in mind that the project implementation period is 9months. Compose an initial draft, and develop a comprehensive budget based on eligible costs. Clearly define your objectives by establishing specific milestones. Step 3: Draft Responses Prepare your answers for each section of the “Standardized Application Form Template” document, before starting the online submission. Step 4: Prepare Mandatory Documents Complete and sign the following required forms: Complete the “Tables with Activities, Budget, Milestones, and Risks” document. Please note that milestones may be subject to negotiation if the proposal is selected, and applicants will not be evaluated based on the proposed milestones Fill in the “SME and Eligibility Declaration form”. Fill in the “Funding eligibility and absence of conflict of interest declaration form”. Step 5: Complete the Online Form Access the online portal – EU Survey to input your responses. We recommend using a stable internet connection to prevent data loss. Step 6: Upload Attachments Attach all mandatory documents from Step 4 into their respective upload fields within the form. You can also contact: fpt.eu.helpdesk [at] gmail.com (fpt[dot]eu[dot]helpdesk[at]gmail[dot]com) COSME Share this Article

analysis.objeto_y_actuaciones: La convocatoria financia capacitación, mentoría técnica y desarrollo de currícula de formación para 40 PYME del sector textil en transformación digital, economía circular y producción sostenible, con duración de 9 meses y presupuesto máximo de €50.000 por beneficiaria. Excluye explícitamente a clusters, organizaciones intermediarias y consorcios; cada solicitante debe representar una única PYME legalmente constituida en países participantes en el Single Market Programme, con al menos un miembro del equipo que hable inglés.
analysis.resumen: Kalfrisa no es elegible. La convocatoria Single Market Programme (SMP) está reservada a PYME que operen en la cadena de valor textil (NACE C13, C14, C15.12, C22.19, C38, J62, J63, C28.94). El perfil de Kalfrisa (CNAE 2899, fabricación de maquinaria industrial para procesos térmicos en cerámica, siderurgia, metalurgia, vidrio, química, cemento, etc.) no coincide con el sector textil. Aunque la convocatoria admite empresas de sectores complementarios si su innovación contribuye directamente a textil, no consta evidencia de que Kalfrisa tenga experiencia, clientes o proyectos en ese sector. Además, la oportunidad se centra en capacitación y mentoría para transformación digital y sostenibilidad textil, no en desarrollo de tecnología térmica industrial.
analysis.accion: Descartar. Kalfrisa no cumple el requisito fundamental de operar en la cadena de valor textil. No procede presentar candidatura.
analysis.motivo_descarte: Kalfrisa (CNAE 2899, fabricación de maquinaria industrial) no opera en la cadena de valor textil. La convocatoria exige que las PYME sean «operating in the textile value chain» con NACE codes específicos (C13.1-C13.3, C13.9, C14.1, C14.3, C15.12, C22.19, C38, J62, J63, C28.94). Aunque se admiten empresas de sectores complementarios (tecnología, maquinaria) si la innovación contribuye directamente a la cadena textil, no consta evidencia de que Kalfrisa tenga clientes o proyectos en textil. Su perfil se centra en procesos térmicos industriales (cerámica, siderurgia, metalurgia, vidrio, química, cemento, etc.), ajeno al sector textil.

raw_document.description: Opportunity PowerUp NetZero Open Call for Innovation Projects DEADLINE: 15 September 2026 Purpose of the Call The PowerUp NetZero Open Call for Innovation Projects provides financial support to SMEs and start-ups seeking to adopt, develop, or improve net-zero technologies and solutions within their processes, products, or services. The call focuses on specific topics and challenges addressing the following Net-Zero technologies: Solar Energy Battery and Energy Storage Hydrogen Technologies Sustainable Biogas and Biomethane Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS) Scope of Supported Projects The call targets collaborative innovation projects aimed at: Developing and testing Proofs of Concept (PoC) for new or improved environmentally friendly products; Implementing innovative net-zero solutions and services; Conducting pilot and demonstration activities. Funding Conditions Total available budget: EUR 1,615,000 Number of supported projects: at least 14 projects Grant amount provided by PowerUp NetZero per project proposal: between EUR 80,000 and EUR 120,000 (covering up to 80% of the total project budget) Consortium composition: minimum 2 and maximum 3 companies Beneficiaries must provide at least 20% co-financing through private resources. Innovation Requirements A high degree of innovation is expected from all proposed projects. Funded activities may address technical risks associated with the demonstration of innovative technologies and solutions, including: Optimisation of technology processes and operational parameters. Improvement of product, service, or solution characteristics. Technology Readiness Level Innovation projects should demonstrate an innovative net-zero technology or solution in an operational or in a Virtual & Industrially Relevant environment (TRL 6-7) but are not necessarily expected yet to reach large scale demonstration or commercial production. Eligibility Criteria Applicants must be Consortia of SMEs (also including start-ups provided they are SMEs) established in an EU Member State or in a country participating in the Single Market Programme (SMP) at the moment of the call launching date.Applicants must have at least one closed and validated financial year." Further Information Official call webpage: https://piemonteinnova.it/second-powerup-netzero-open-call-innovation-p… COSME Batteries biogas energy storage European SMEs Hydrogen Innovation low-carbon economy circular resource efficiency Solar energy Share this Article

related_document_contents.description: Power Up Net Zero Second Open Call - Fondazione Piemonte Innova Iscriviti alla Newsletter Chi siamo Governance Il team Lavora con noi Sostenibilità Certificazioni Storia Ecosistema Il Polo di innovazione ICT Il sistema dei poli Il Cluster Nazionale Smart Communities Il sistema dei Cluster Nazionali EEN – Enterprise Europe Network Diventa partner Cosa Facciamo FPI per città e territori FPI in Europa Servizi GDPR e Compliance Cybersecurity e Dati AI e Digitalizzazione Supporto progettuale Servizi finanziati Progetti Bandi News & Eventi Power Up Net Zero Open Call FOR innovation projects The PowerUp NetZero OPEN CALL FOR INNOVATION PROJECTS provides financial support for helping SMEs and start-ups adopt or improve net-zero technologies and solutions (Solar energy, Battery and energy storage, H2 technologies, Sustainable biogas and biomethane, Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)) in their processes, products or services. The call for innovation projects targets companies working together to implement: PoC or testing of new / improved environmentally friendly products; N et-zero solutions and services; P ilot /demonstration actions. A high degree of innovation is expected in response of this call. Funded activities could address technical risks associated with the demonstration of innovative technologies and solutions, such as optimising technology processes and operational parameters and/or improving the characteristics of their products/solutions. Innovation projects should demonstrate an innovative net-zero technology or solution in an operational or in a Virtual & Industrially Relevant environment (TRL 6-7) but are not necessarily expected yet to reach large scale demonstration or commercial production. Applicants must be Consortia of SMEs (also including start-ups provided they are SMEs) established in an EU Member State or in a country participating in the Single Market Programme (SMP) at the moment of the call launching date. GUIDELINES TO APPLY KEY DATES Call opening date: 18-06-2026 Call deadline: 15-09-2026 at 17:00 (Brussels time) The application form is available here. Templates of the supporting documents to successfully complete an application can be downloaded here: Supporting Documents Templates . In relation to the Strand B: City of Turin Challenges, the City of Turin has shared the following factsheets with specific information on their main challenges of interest: City of Turin – Po River Test Area – Fact Sheet City of Turin – Urban Road Test Area- Fact Sheet City of Turin – Catalytic-Pavements-Test-Area WHO CAN APPLY? Applications must be presented by a Consortia composed by at least 2 SMEs or start-ups and maximum 3 SMES. All SMEs should have at least one closed and validated financial year and registered in an EU Member State or a country participating in the Single Market Programme (SMP). Each SME may participate to only one Consortia, and each Consortia may submit only one application to this call. In the case of multiple submissions by the same applicant, only the last one received (as per timestamp of the IT system) will enter the evaluation process, the rest will not be considered, meaning, they will be declared non-eligible. WHAT ARE THE ACTIVITIES TO BE ADDRESSED WITHIN THE PROPOSAL? Funding will be provided to SMEs and start-ups for activities related to development, implementation, adoption, test and/or demonstration of solutions related to at least one of the NZT tackled by the project and answering to specific challenges within the following topics: STRAND 1 Topics: 1) Waste management of solar panels and batteries; 2) Materials and critical raw materials concerns; 3) Storage alternatives to batteries; 4) Digital solutions for PowerUp NetZero NZT; 5) Value chain efficiency; 6) CO2 and hydrogen coupling; and 7) Carbon capture technologies. STRAND 2: City of Turin Challenges All activities must have linkages with at least one of the project’s 5 Net-Zero Technologies (Solar energy, Battery and energy storage, H2 technologies, Sustainable biogas/ biomethane, and Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)). WHAT’S THE AVAILABLE BUDGET? PowerUp NetZero has allocated EUR 1.615.000,00 to support Innovation Projects , with financial support for at least 14 projects. The budget is managed by two consortium partners: FPI and EnviPark. The financial contribution per project proposal ranges from a minimum of EUR 80.000,00 to a maximum of EUR 120.000,00. Projects must be submitted by consortia composed of at least two members and no more than three companies and must address at least one of the challenges described in this document. Beneficiaries must ensure a minimum co-funding rate of 20% of the total eligible budget of the supported activity, to be covered through private financial sources. Applicants should plan budgets in line with the co-funding rate applicable to the requested grant amount. HOW LONG SHOULD THE ACTIVITY LAST? All activities financed by this call must have a duration of maximum 10 months starting from the signature of the contract. WHAT DO I NEED TO SUBMIT AN APPLICATION? All needed information is available at the Call Guidelines above. The application form is available at the EUSurvey Platform. A word template is available as a guide of the application form, but it must not be considered an application. While all supporting documents to successfully complete an application are found here: Supporting Documents templates . Only one application per SME will be accepted under this specific call. If an entity submits more than one proposal, as a general rule, only the first proposal submitted will be considered eligible for evaluation. Beneficiaries can participate to the different Open Calls of the project (Business Innovation Services and Technology Adoption Activities or Innovation Projects), but a single beneficiary cannot receive more than 60.000,00 EUR overall. Q&A & Presentations For any inquiries, reach out t o punz@piemonteinnova.it English Info Day recording Italian Info Day Presentation. Las capacidades de Kalfrisa en recuperación de calor residual, hornos industriales híbridos e hibridación térmica no encajan en los temas obligatorios listados. Aunque Kalfrisa posee experiencia en hidrógeno (mezclas H2 y demostraciones hasta 100% H2), la convocatoria requiere que el proyecto demuestre una tecnología neto-cero en entorno operativo o industrialmente relevante (TRL 6-7) alineada con uno de los cinco temas neto-cero. Sin evidencia de que Kalfrisa desarrolle soluciones de hidrógeno como tecnología neto-cero independiente (no como combustible para procesos térmicos propios), la elegibilidad permanece desconocida. Además, la convocatoria exige consorcio de 2-3 SMEs; no se proporcionan candidatos de socio.

Aunque Kalfrisa posee experiencia en hidrógeno, se aplica como combustible para procesos térmicos, no como vector energético neto-cero independiente. Consorcio obligatorio sin socios identificados, presupuesto muy reducido (EUR 120.000), y plazo corto (26 días) hacen la acción inviable. Recomendar explorar convocatorias de I+D industrial en eficiencia térmica, recuperación de calor o hibridación de procesos (Horizon Europe, LIFE, Innovation Fund, CDTI, IDAE) donde Kalfrisa pueda actuar como líder tecnológico o demostrador industrial.

Requiere verificación de ejercicio financiero cerrado y validado. La desalineación temática es crítica y no superable sin reposicionamiento radical del proyecto.
analysis.accion: Descartar. PowerUp NetZero no es compatible con el perfil de Kalfrisa. La convocatoria se enfoca en tecnologías neto-cero específicas (Solar, Baterías, Almacenamiento, Hidrógeno, Biogás, CCS) en demostración TRL 6-7; las capacidades de Kalfrisa en recuperación de calor residual, hornos industriales híbridos e hibridación térmica no encajan en los temas obligatorios. Aunque Kalfrisa posee experiencia en hidrógeno, se aplica como combustible para procesos térmicos, no como vector energético neto-cero independiente. Consorcio obligatorio sin socios identificados, presupuesto muy reducido (EUR 120.000), y plazo corto (26 días) hacen la acción inviable. Recomendar explorar convocatorias de I+D industrial en eficiencia térmica, recuperación de calor o hibridación de procesos (Horizon Europe, LIFE, Innovation Fund, CDTI, IDAE) donde Kalfrisa pueda actuar como líder tecnológico o demostrador industrial.

raw_document.title: GRAPPA Open Call for valorisation of agri-food biomass side-streams - CUT-OFF 2
raw_document.description: Opportunity GRAPPA Open Call for valorisation of agri-food biomass side-streams - CUT-OFF 2 DEADLINE: 20 October 2026 GRAPPA call targets SME projects developing solutions that increase the valorisation of biomass side-streams into the development, adoption, and commercialisation of innovative upcycled ingredients SCOPE AND ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS This call targets innovative SMEs developing solutions that increase the valorisation of biomass side-streams , contributing to more sustainable and resilient agri-food ecosystems through the development of new processes, services and products. This Innovation Call includes financial support for projects especially focusing on the development, adoption, and commercialisation of innovative upcycled ingredients for food and non-food applications, products, business processes, and technologies (including digital) that maximise the valorisation of agri-food biomass and side-streams . These projects should have a minimum Technology Readiness Level (TRL) of 6. The Innovation Open Call targets: SMEs in the agri-food production and/or processing sector; SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector; SMEs in other sectors (ex. cosmetics, nutraceuticals, etc) that valorise their own biomass/by-products/side-streams for the agri-food sector; SMEs offering solutions and/or technology for the valorisation of biomass/by-products/side-streams from the agri-food sector (development and application of new technologies or processes). Applicants can be SMEs registered at EU Member States and countries associated to the Single Market Programme TIMING Launch of the Open Call: March 26, 2026 First Cut-off date: May 26, 2026 – 17:00 CET Second Cut-off date: October 20, 2026 – 17:00 CET SUBMISSION AND EVALUATION PROCESS AMENDED CALL TEXT 16 JULY 2026 : Please take into account that the Open call documentation has been updated. Submission of your proposal has to be done on the GRAPPA call website: Click here Your proposal will be submitted to an eligibility check, if all the mandatory information is completed your proposal will be evaluated. The evaluation will be done by 3 independent evaluators following a clear and transparent evaluation procedure that you can find in the Grappa open call applicant’s guide available at the call website . This evaluation period shall take place within two months after the closure of each cut-off date. Top-ranked proposals that meet the threshold scores will be awarded and contacted immediately after the final ranking and enter the Sub-Grant Agreement phase which shall last approximately one month. FURTHER INFORMATION You can consult to the GRAPPA Open Call Documentation, including the Open call applicant’s guide and Application Form at the call website For further information about this Call, you can consult the open call applicant’s guide that provide all the necessary information about this call. For more information about the overall GRAPPA project, you can consult our website and LinkedIn page . TASK DESCRIPTION The applicant’s project must lead to the implementation of either a new process, a new product, or a new service or a combination of them . Proposals can be submitted either by a single SME or by an SMEs consortium with up to three (3) SMEs . Projects must have a minimum Technology Readiness Level ( TRL ) of at least 6. The expected duration of the innovation projects is of 1 year . For Single SME projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (1 SME) is €60.000 . For collaborative projects, the maximum lump-sum grant per project (2-3 SMEs) is €90.000 . This call has a total budget of € 2.020.000 over both cut-off dates. Innovation grants must be matched by at least 15% private financial contribution (debt or own financial resources), with proof required. AMENDMENT 16 JULY 2026 Following aspects of the call text have been updated and clarified: Thematic priorities - scope of the call and valorisation pathways Call definitions: biosolutions added, TRL requirements clarified Documents required: no stamp needed, only signature Eligibility criteria Evaluation procedure, criteria and scoring: 2 stage evaluation process in Cut-off 2, pre-selection (knock-out stage) added. Timing of the evaluation procedure cut-off 2 prolonged Re-submission of proposals: to be done in new application form Period to file complaints SPOC contact details Pay attention that there is an adapted application form for cut-off 2! raw_document.title: Eurostars Call 11 for projects - deadline September 2026
raw_document.description: Summary Profile Type Research & Development Request POD Reference RDRGR20260731019 Term of Validity 31 July 2026 - 31 July 2027 Company's Country Greece Type of partnership Research and development cooperation agreement Targeted Countries All countries For more information contact the EEN partner nearest to you. Express interest Find my local partner General information Short Summary A Greek innovative SME developing artificial intelligence-based media intelligence and broadcast-monitoring technologies is preparing a Eurostars Call 11 project. The 24-month project will advance a pilot-validated platform into a scalable, multilingual and rights-aware European solution. Media, rights-management, AI, software and research partners are sought for R&D, pilots and validation. Full Description A Greek innovative SME is preparing an international research and development project under Eurostars Call 11. The project, provisionally titled PULSE-EU, will advance a pilot-validated media-intelligence pipeline for audio, video and text from technology readiness level (TRL) 6 to TRL 8 over 24 months. Media organisations process large volumes of unstructured audiovisual content, but existing tools are often fragmented: transcription, content identification, semantic analysis, visual analysis and rights metadata are handled separately. Outputs are frequently generic, difficult to adapt to each organisation and not ready for editorial, monitoring, licensing or rights-management workflows. The project will research and develop a scalable European platform that converts audiovisual content into configurable, machine-readable intelligence. It will extend client-defined templates, controlled vocabularies and taxonomies; multilingual extraction and cross-language rendering; distributed worker orchestration; privately deployed or self-hosted artificial intelligence; and editorial-grade structured outputs. Research may also cover direct visual-stream analysis, including optical character recognition, scene and shot detection, logo or product recognition and temporal correlation of visual findings with speech, sound, transcripts and content-identification results. A rights-aware workstream will investigate interoperability between detected recordings, musical works, rightsholders, publishers and identifiers such as ISRC, ISWC and IPI. This may support metadata validation, recording-to-work matching and future cue-sheet workflows without replacing partners' existing rights or royalty systems. The Greek SME will contribute its existing configurable platform, audio fingerprinting and broadcast-monitoring technology, self-hosted AI and owned computing infrastructure, Greek-language media-intelligence know-how, APIs, template and vocabulary architecture, and pilot-validation capacity. Its pre-existing platform and related technology will remain background intellectual property; project access rights and ownership of jointly developed results will be defined in the consortium agreement. Partners are sought from Eurostars countries, particularly organisations active in media, broadcasting, publishing, music technology, rights management, multilingual AI, computer vision, scalable software or audiovisual data. They will undertake complementary R&D and/or provide datasets, integration environments, pilots, validation and routes to market. The consortium will be led by an innovative SME and will include at least two independent organisations from at least two Eurostars countries. Expressions of interest are requested by 20 August 2026. The Eurostars Call 11 deadline is 10 September 2026 at 14:00 CEST. Advantages and Innovations The project starts from a prototype already tested in relevant media and broadcast environments (TRL 6), rather than from a concept. This reduces technical risk and allows partners to test new research results directly through existing APIs, workflows, configurable templates, monitoring infrastructure and realistic audiovisual datasets. Its principal innovation is the unification of capabilities that are normally deployed as separate tools. Audio fingerprinting, broadcast monitoring, speech processing, semantic analysis, multilingual rendering, visual understanding and rights metadata will be correlated through common timestamps and transformed into structured, machine-readable outputs. Unlike fixed-purpose analysis products, the platform is designed around client-defined attributes, controlled vocabularies, taxonomies and output schemas. The same technical core can therefore support different editorial, agency, broadcaster, publisher and rights-holder workflows without developing a separate product for every use case. The planned multilingual R&D gives particular attention to Greek and other European or less-resourced languages. Self-hosted and private deployment options can support confidentiality, data protection and European technological sovereignty requirements. For music and audiovisual rights applications, the project aims to connect detected recordings with works, contributors, ownership data and identifiers. This creates a practical bridge between content detection and metadata or cue-sheet workflows while allowing rights platforms to retain their existing systems. The target outcome is a validated, internationally scalable product, service and process ready for commercial deployment at TRL 8. Technical Specification or Expertise Sought Relevant partners should contribute at least one of the following: 1. Media, broadcast, publishing, record-label, music-library or rights-management pilot environments, including representative audiovisual content, metadata, workflow requirements, validation criteria and end-user feedback. 2. Multilingual speech and language technologies for speech-to-text, diarisation, transcript correction, translation, entity extraction, semantic classification and cross-language rendering, with measurable performance in Greek and/or other European languages. API, licensed or self-hosted deployment should be possible. 3. Computer-vision or multimodal expertise for scene and shot detection, optical character recognition, on-screen text, logo/product detection, visual context and timestamped fusion of image, speech, sound and transcript results. 4. Scalable software and data-engineering expertise for distributed processing, worker orchestration, secure APIs, metadata interchange, quality assurance and deployment at European scale. 5. Music-rights, repertoire, publishing, royalty-accounting or cue-sheet expertise, with documented data models or interfaces for recordings, works, rightsholders, territories, ownership shares and identifiers including ISRC, ISWC and IPI. Recording-to-work matching and the handling of incomplete or conflicting metadata are particularly relevant. Proposed work must complement the existing platform and provide high reuse. The project does not seek a replacement audio-fingerprinting, monitoring or generic analysis platform, nor unrelated product development. Stage of Development Under development Sustainable Development Goals Goal 16: Peace and Justice Strong Institutions Goal 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth Goal 9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure Goal 17: Partnerships to achieve the Goal IPR status Secret know-how Partner Sought Expected Role of a Partner The consortium seeks complementary partners under a research and development cooperation agreement. Media agencies, broadcasters, publishers, record labels, production-music libraries and rights-management organizations may act as validation, demonstration and commercialization partners. They should define operational use cases, provide lawful access to representative content and metadata, support integration, evaluate accuracy and usability, and validate the solution in editorial, monitoring, advertising, licensing or rights workflows. Artificial intelligence, natural-language processing and multilingual technology companies may contribute models, datasets and adaptation expertise for speech recognition, diarisation, transcript processing, translation, entity extraction, semantic analysis and cross-language rendering. They should support technical benchmarking and integration through APIs or deployable components. Computer-vision and multimodal partners may research scene, shot, optical character recognition, on-screen graphics, logo/product and visual-context analysis. Their role will be to produce timestamped visual detections and connect them with audio, transcript and fingerprinting results. Software and data-engineering partners may contribute distributed processing, secure interoperability, performance testing and scalable deployment. Rights, metadata and cue-sheet platforms may provide data structures, identifiers, matching mechanisms, exchange interfaces and pilot environments for connecting recordings, works, rightsholders and publishers. Universities and research organisations may contribute multilingual datasets, applied AI research, computer vision, metadata matching, evaluation methods and independent validation. Commercial partners should also help define exploitation routes and access to European or international markets. Each partner is expected to lead clearly defined tasks, allocate qualified personnel, contribute an eligible project budget and participate in joint technical validation and dissemination. Partners will retain their pre-existing intellectual property. Access rights to background technology and ownership or licensing of jointly developed results will be agreed in the consortium agreement. The Greek SME is prepared to coordinate as the innovative SME lead, while a core-technology role within a strong partner-led consortium may also be considered. related_document_contents.description: Summary Profile Type Research & Development Request POD Reference RDRTR20260820005 Term of Validity 20 August 2026 - 20 August 2027 Company's Country Türkiye Type of partnership Research and development cooperation agreement Targeted Countries Finland Poland Portugal France Denmark Spain Netherlands Czechia Ireland For more information contact the EEN partner nearest to you. Express interest Find my local partner General information Short Summary The company develops OrthoAI, an AI platform that screens skeletal malocclusion and mouth-breathing risk in children (ages 4-8) from a single facial photograph, reviewed by a licensed orthodontist. Backed by an EU Seal of Excellence and a Harvard Capstone collaboration, the project is preparing a Eurostars Call 11 submission and seeks R&D partners to strengthen its AI/computer vision, software/data engineering, and clinical validation work packages. Full Description OrthoAI is an AI-based screening tool that analyses skeletal malocclusion risk and mouth-breathing risk in children aged 4-8 from a single facial photograph. Every AI output is reviewed by a licensed orthodontist before any clinical recommendation is made, positioning the platform as a clinician-reviewed screening and communication aid rather than a standalone diagnostic device. The project builds on the team's own published machine learning study (524 children aged 5-12, over 81% accuracy in single-photograph skeletal malocclusion screening), giving it a strong clinical and scientific evidence base. The project has also received an EU Seal of Excellence and was developed in part through a Harvard Capstone Project. The current consortium includes: • An SME (Turkey) — coordinator, product and AI development • A university (Turkey) — clinical execution • A university (Italy) — scientific and methodological leadership, with the team led by the current President of the World Federation of Orthodontists The company is now preparing a submission to Eurostars Call 11 (deadline 10 September 2026) and is looking for one or more additional R&D partners to join the consortium as full beneficiaries (not subcontractors) contributing real technical work and their own project budget. This also helps the consortium meet Eurostars budget-distribution rules (no single country above 70% of total costs). Priority areas of interest for partners: • Applied AI / computer vision expertise to strengthen model robustness, generalisability across diverse populations, and validation of the screening algorithm • Software engineering and data engineering capacity to support data infrastructure, systems integration, and production-grade deployment • Clinical or regulatory-adjacent expertise relevant to paediatric digital health tools (welcome but not mandatory, as this is currently subcontracted separately) The ideal partner is based in a Eurostars country with confirmed national budget for the September 2026 call. Advantages and Innovations OrthoAI combines a validated scientific foundation with a clear, narrow regulatory positioning: • Evidence base: built on the team's own published study (524 children, 5-12 years, over 81% accuracy in single-photograph skeletal malocclusion classification) — a real, peer-reviewed clinical evidence base rather than a concept-stage idea. • Recognition: EU Seal of Excellence; developed in part through a Harvard Capstone collaboration. • Clinical credibility: scientific leadership team includes the current President of the World Federation of Orthodontists. • Clean regulatory scope: positioned consistently as a clinician-reviewed screening and communication aid, not a standalone diagnostic device, reducing MDR classification risk and reviewer scepticism. • Real-world relevance: addresses an underdiagnosed paediatric condition (mouth-breathing and skeletal malocclusion) using only a smartphone photograph, making screening accessible outside specialist orthodontic settings. • Market potential: designed for integration into paediatric and orthodontic clinical workflows across Europe, with a clinician-in-the-loop model. Technical Specification or Expertise Sought The consortium is seeking R&D partners with strong technical expertise in either AI/Computer Vision or Software/Data Engineering to contribute to the development and validation of a digital health screening solution. For the AI/Computer Vision profile, expertise is sought in applied artificial intelligence, image processing, pattern recognition and computer vision, particularly in developing robust and generalisable models. The partner should be able to contribute to algorithm development, optimisation, explainability and validation across diverse populations, including variations in age, ethnicity and image quality. Experience in medical imaging or digital health applications would be an advantage. For the Software/Data Engineering profile, expertise is sought in full-stack development, systems integration, backend infrastructure and data engineering. Relevant capabilities include the development of secure and scalable data pipelines, APIs, dashboards and clinician-facing interfaces suitable for a regulated digital health environment. The selected partner(s) will be expected to take responsibility for a clearly defined technical work package, contribute to system development and integration, support technical validation and testing, and participate in dissemination activities. Experience in developing production-grade, interoperable and secure digital health solutions, including consideration of data protection and regulatory requirements, would be particularly valuable. Stage of Development Under development Sustainable Development Goals Goal 3: Good Health and Well-being Goal 9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure IPR status IPR granted IPR notes The core intellectual property underlying the proposed solution is protected. A patent covering the AI-based system for the early diagnosis of skeletal orthodontic malocclusions has been granted/registered, with international patent protection pursued in multiple jurisdictions. The project will build upon this existing protected technology while generating additional foreground IP related to further AI development, clinical validation, digital therapeutic functionalities and regulatory-compliant implementation. Ownership and exploitation of newly generated IP will be defined among project partners according to their respective contributions and the consortium agreement. Partner Sought Expected Role of a Partner The company is seeking one or more R&D partners to join the Eurostars Call 11 consortium as full beneficiaries, contributing real technical work and their own project budget (not as subcontractors). Priority profile 1 — AI / Computer Vision partner: • Applied AI, computer vision, image processing and/or pattern recognition expertise • Experience taking models from feasibility through prototyping to production-grade deployment • Ability to contribute to model robustness, generalisability across diverse populations (age, ethnicity, image quality), and validation/explainability of the screening algorithm • Ideally, though not required, some experience in health or medical imaging applications Priority profile 2 — Software / Data Engineering partner: • Full-stack software development, systems integration, and/or data engineering expertise • Experience building data pipelines, dashboards, or backend infrastructure suitable for a regulated digital health product • Interest in contributing to production-grade software architecture supporting the AI model and clinician-facing workflow Both partner types would be expected to: • Take ownership of a defined technical work package within the Eurostars project • Contribute to proposal preparation, technical development, validation, and dissemination activities • Bring their own project budget from a Eurostars country with confirmed national funding for the September 2026 call • Provide timely input on their work package description and required partner documentation ahead of the 10 September 2026 deadline Their team leads the overall Eurostars application, platform submission (myeurekaproject.org), and coordination with national funding bodies, supported by our proposal-writing partner, so partners are not required to navigate the application platform themselves or manage the overall submission; their focus is on defining and delivering their technical work package. They are open to discussing consortium structure, work package definition, and budget allocation directly with interested partners. It will extend client-defined templates, controlled vocabularies and taxonomies; multilingual extraction and cross-language rendering; distributed worker orchestration; privately deployed or self-hosted artificial intelligence; and editorial-grade structured outputs. Research may also cover direct visual-stream analysis, including optical character recognition, scene and shot detection, logo or product recognition and temporal correlation of visual findings with speech, sound, transcripts and content-identification results. A rights-aware workstream will investigate interoperability between detected recordings, musical works, rightsholders, publishers and identifiers such as ISRC, ISWC and IPI. This may support metadata validation, recording-to-work matching and future cue-sheet workflows without replacing partners' existing rights or royalty systems. The Greek SME will contribute its existing configurable platform, audio fingerprinting and broadcast-monitoring technology, self-hosted AI and owned computing infrastructure, Greek-language media-intelligence know-how, APIs, template and vocabulary architecture, and pilot-validation capacity. Its pre-existing platform and related technology will remain background intellectual property; project access rights and ownership of jointly developed results will be defined in the consortium agreement. Partners are sought from Eurostars countries, particularly organisations active in media, broadcasting, publishing, music technology, rights management, multilingual AI, computer vision, scalable software or audiovisual data. They will undertake complementary R&D and/or provide datasets, integration environments, pilots, validation and routes to market. The consortium will be led by an innovative SME and will include at least two independent organisations from at least two Eurostars countries. Expressions of interest are requested by 20 August 2026. The Eurostars Call 11 deadline is 10 September 2026 at 14:00 CEST. Advantages and Innovations The project starts from a prototype already tested in relevant media and broadcast environments (TRL 6), rather than from a concept. This reduces technical risk and allows partners to test new research results directly through existing APIs, workflows, configurable templates, monitoring infrastructure and realistic audiovisual datasets. Its principal innovation is the unification of capabilities that are normally deployed as separate tools. Audio fingerprinting, broadcast monitoring, speech processing, semantic analysis, multilingual rendering, visual understanding and rights metadata will be correlated through common timestamps and transformed into structured, machine-readable outputs. Unlike fixed-purpose analysis products, the platform is designed around client-defined attributes, controlled vocabularies, taxonomies and output schemas. The same technical core can therefore support different editorial, agency, broadcaster, publisher and rights-holder workflows without developing a separate product for every use case. The planned multilingual R&D gives particular attention to Greek and other European or less-resourced languages. Self-hosted and private deployment options can support confidentiality, data protection and European technological sovereignty requirements. For music and audiovisual rights applications, the project aims to connect detected recordings with works, contributors, ownership data and identifiers. This creates a practical bridge between content detection and metadata or cue-sheet workflows while allowing rights platforms to retain their existing systems. The target outcome is a validated, internationally scalable product, service and process ready for commercial deployment at TRL 8. Technical Specification or Expertise Sought Relevant partners should contribute at least one of the following: 1. Media, broadcast, publishing, record-label, music-library or rights-management pilot environments, including representative audiovisual content, metadata, workflow requirements, validation criteria and end-user feedback. 2. Multilingual speech and language technologies for speech-to-text, diarisation, transcript correction, translation, entity extraction, semantic classification and cross-language rendering, with measurable performance in Greek and/or other European languages. API, licensed or self-hosted deployment should be possible. 3. Computer-vision or multimodal expertise for scene and shot detection, optical character recognition, on-screen text, logo/product detection, visual context and timestamped fusion of image, speech, sound and transcript results. 4. Scalable software and data-engineering expertise for distributed processing, worker orchestration, secure APIs, metadata interchange, quality assurance and deployment at European scale. 5. Music-rights, repertoire, publishing, royalty-accounting or cue-sheet expertise, with documented data models or interfaces for recordings, works, rightsholders, territories, ownership shares and identifiers including ISRC, ISWC and IPI. Recording-to-work matching and the handling of incomplete or conflicting metadata are particularly relevant. Proposed work must complement the existing platform and provide high reuse. The project does not seek a replacement audio-fingerprinting, monitoring or generic analysis platform, nor unrelated product development. raw_document.description: Summary Profile Type Research & Development Request POD Reference RDRPL20260716014 Term of Validity 16 July 2026 - 16 July 2027 Company's Country Poland Type of partnership Research and development cooperation agreement Targeted Countries Norway Iceland Liechtenstein For more information contact the EEN partner nearest to you. Express interest Find my local partner General information Short Summary A Polish research organisation is preparing a proposal under the POLNORIS Call within the Applied Research and Innovation Programme, financed by the EEA Grants 2021–2028. The project will develop biodegradable biocomposites from modified PLA and recycled cotton textile waste. Partners from Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein are sought, especially textile recyclers, LCA and biodegradation experts, and industrial end users, for R&D cooperation. Full Description A Polish research organisation is preparing a project proposal under the POLNORIS Call for Proposals, implemented within the Applied Research and Innovation Programme and financed by the EEA Financial Mechanism 2021–2028. The Programme Operator is the National Centre for Research and Development in Poland. The POLNORIS Call aims to enhance the quality of research in Poland and strengthen international cooperation in research and innovation through projects implemented jointly by Polish organisations and partners from the Donor States: Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein. The call is open to different thematic areas, but proposals must contribute to at least one of the three priorities of the EEA Grants: the European green transition; democracy, rule of law and human rights; or social inclusion and resilience. The proposed project directly contributes to the European green transition and circular-economy objectives. The research organisation intends to develop biodegradable biocomposites based on recycled cotton fibres and biodegradable polymer matrices, including modified PLA, to address the environmental impact of textile waste and the need for more sustainable materials. The concept builds on previous research in fibre-matrix interface engineering and polymer modification. It aims to improve compatibility between hydrophilic natural fibres and biodegradable polymers. Waste cotton fibres obtained from post-consumer or post-industrial textile streams will be used as reinforcement in place of conventional natural fibres. The planned work will focus on targeted modification of the polymer matrix and optimisation of fibre-matrix interactions. The objective is to develop materials with improved mechanical performance, durability and controlled biodegradability, while reducing environmental impact and supporting circular-economy principles. The project will valorise textile waste by converting it into higher-value materials. It will assess environmental performance through life cycle assessment and biodegradability testing and will evaluate scalability, market potential and applicability in selected industrial sectors. The project consortium must include at least one entity established in Poland acting as the Project Promoter and at least one research organisation from Norway, Iceland or Liechtenstein. The Polish Project Promoter may be a research organisation or an enterprise. Additional project partners may include public or private entities, commercial or non-commercial organisations, enterprises, non-governmental organisations and industrial end users established in Poland or in one of the Donor States. The POLNORIS Call supports industrial research and experimental development. Interdisciplinary and cross-sectoral cooperation, research valorisation and the involvement of early-stage researchers are encouraged. Applications may be submitted from 17 September 2026, 10:00 CEST, until 17 December 2026, 15:00 CET. Applications must be prepared in English and submitted electronically. Advantages and Innovations The proposed approach combines recycled cotton textile fibres with targeted polymer modification and fibre-matrix interface engineering. Its innovative aspects include: - use of post-consumer or post-industrial cotton textile waste as a secondary raw material; - tailored modification of the polymer matrix and fibres to improve fibre-matrix compatibility; - development of biodegradable composites with improved mechanical performance and durability; - integration of material development with life cycle assessment and biodegradability testing; - potential for scale-up and use in different industrial sectors. Compared with the simple use of conventional natural fibres, the project focuses on the valorisation of real textile waste streams and on engineering the fibre-matrix interface. This increases the environmental and economic relevance of the resulting material solutions. Technical Specification or Expertise Sought The research organisation seeks partners with complementary expertise for the development, testing, validation and future application of the biocomposites. The following partner profiles are sought: - textile recycling companies experienced in collecting, processing and supplying waste cotton textile materials; - research institutions or specialised organisations with expertise in life cycle assessment, environmental impact assessment and biodegradation testing of materials; - industrial end users interested in testing the developed materials under application conditions, validating their performance and supporting market-oriented activities. The partners should be interested in a research and development project focused on scaling, testing and validation of innovative material solutions. Stage of Development Under development Sustainable Development Goals Goal 13: Climate Action Goal 9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure Goal 12: Responsible Consumption and Production IPR status Secret know-how Partner Sought Expected Role of a Partner The partners will contribute according to their expertise and will take an active role in the development and validation activities. - Textile recycling partners will supply recycled cotton fibres, support their preparation and contribute to the optimisation of raw material streams. - Life cycle assessment and biodegradation partners will evaluate environmental performance, including life cycle impacts and the degradation behaviour of the materials. - Industrial end users will test the materials under application conditions, define performance requirements and validate usability and market relevance. All partners will participate in joint development activities, knowledge exchange and validation of results, contributing to the advancement and application potential of the developed technology. evaluation.eligibility_reason: Kalfrisa está ubicada en España (Zaragoza). La convocatoria EEA Grants 2021–2028 requiere que el Project Promoter esté establecido en Polonia y que al menos una organización de investigación esté establecida en Noruega, Islandia o Liechtenstein. Kalfrisa no cumple ninguno de estos requisitos geográficos obligatorios. Además, los temas requeridos (biocomposites biodegradables, residuos textiles de algodón reciclado, PLA modificado) están completamente fuera del ámbito de procesos térmicos industriales, recuperación de calor residual, combustión, electrificación térmica y valorización de residuos que define el perfil de Kalfrisa.
risks_and_unknowns: Kalfrisa no está ubicada en una geografía elegible (Polonia, Noruega, Islandia o Liechtenstein).
Los temas obligatorios (biocomposites biodegradables, textiles reciclados, PLA) no tienen conexión con las capacidades de Kalfrisa en procesos térmicos industriales.
La convocatoria requiere un consorcio con promotor en Polonia y socio de investigación en un Estado Donante; Kalfrisa no puede cumplir este requisito desde España.
No existe alineación entre las acciones elegibles (ingeniería de interfaz fibra-matriz, modificación de polímeros, ensayos de biodegradabilidad) y la experiencia de Kalfrisa.
evaluation.resumen: Kalfrisa no es elegible. La convocatoria EEA Grants 2021–2028 está restringida geográficamente a Polonia (promotor obligatorio) y Estados Donantes (Noruega, Islandia, Liechtenstein). Kalfrisa, con sede en Zaragoza (España), no cumple estos requisitos territoriales. Además, el ámbito temático (biocomposites biodegradables, residuos textiles, PLA) no tiene conexión alguna con las capacidades de Kalfrisa en procesos térmicos industriales, recuperación de calor residual, combustión con hidrógeno, electrificación térmica ni valorización térmica de residuos. No existe alineación tecnológica ni estratégica.

raw_document.description: SOLICITA ESTA AYUDA DE FORMA TELEMÁTICA INNTERCONECTA - STEP 2026 La actuación denominada "Consorcios Regionales (INNTERCONECTA STEP) tiene como objetivo la financiación de proyectos de I+D en cooperación, con un enfoque regional, liderados por empresas, que persigan una investigación relevante basada en tecnologías disruptivas y que propongan soluciones a desafíos estratégicos en el ámbito de las Tecnologías Estratégicas para Europa (STEP). Con la convocatoria INNTERCONECTA STEP se pretende mejorar el posicionamiento estratégico y competitivo de la industria española, al tiempo que se fomenta la cooperación público-privada. PRÓXIMA APERTURA: OCTUBRE 2026. ACCEDE A NUESTRAS Instrucciones y Manuales de Justificación de Ayudas CDTI Convocatorias INNTERCONECTA - STEP Ficha resumen de la ayuda Actuación INNTERCONECTA - STEP Objetivo general de la actuación Financiación de proyectos de I+D en cooperación, liderados por empresas, desarrollados en uno de los ámbitos tecnológicos STEP: A) Tecnologías digitales: incluidas las del Programa Estratégico de la Década Digital para 20230. B) Tecnologías limpias y eficientes en el uso de los recursos: definidas en el Reglamento sobre la Industria de Cero Emisiones Netas. C) Biotecnología: incluidos los medicamentos que figuran en la lista de la Unión de medicamentos esenciales y sus componentes. Tipo de convocatoria Concurrencia competitiva con plazos determinados de presentación. Estado de la convocatoria Próxima apertura. Tipo de la ayuda Subvención. related_document_contents.description: III. OTRAS DISPOSICIONES MINISTERIO DE CIENCIA, INNOVACIÓN Y UNIVERSIDADES 8122 Orden CNU/331/2026, de 8 de abril, por la que se modifica la Orden CNU/161/2025, de 7 de febrero, por la que se aprueban las bases reguladoras para la concesión de ayudas públicas por el Centro para el Desarrollo Tecnológico y la Innovación, E.P.E., en el marco del Plan Estatal de Investigación Científica y Técnica y de Innovación 2024-2027. A través de esta orden se modifica la Orden CNU/161/2025, de 7 de febrero, por la que se aprueban las bases reguladoras para la concesión de ayudas públicas por el Centro para el Desarrollo Tecnológico y la Innovación, E.P.E. (CDTI) en el marco del Plan Estatal de Investigación Científica y Técnica y de innovación 2024-2027 (en adelante, PEICTI), con la finalidad de introducir y regular una nueva modalidad de ayudas en forma de premios. De conformidad con lo previsto en el programa de trabajo de 2026 del PEICTI, se atribuye al CDTI, en su condición de agente de financiación conforme a la Ley 14/2011, de 1 de junio, de la Ciencia, la Tecnología y la Innovación, la gestión de un nuevo programa de ayudas en forma de premios. La Orden CNU/161/2025, de 7 de febrero, que  […] ras de todas las ayudas del PEICTI gestionadas por el CDTI, solo contempla subvenciones, por lo que resulta precisa su modificación para regular el procedimiento de concesión de las ayudas en forma de premios. Adicionalmente, la experiencia obtenida tras la tramitación de varias convocatorias al amparo de la Orden CNU 161/2025, de 7 de febrero, aconseja una revisión de las bases reguladoras, con el fin de facilitar y simplificar la gestión de estas, introducir determinadas precisiones para evitar dudas interpretativas y mejorar así la seguridad jurídica. Así, se clarifica la definición de determinados beneficiarios, sus obligaciones, se aclara la elegibilidad de las tasas y se amplía la categoría de entidades colaboradoras, entre otras. También se armonizan los umbrales de los criterios de evaluación de las distintas actuaciones con el fin de homogeneizar su aplicación. Otro de los objetivos de esta modificación es asegurar un mayor alineamiento respecto del Reglamento (UE) 651/2014, de 17 de junio, por el que se declaran determinadas categorías de ayudas compatibles con el mercado interior en aplicación de los artículos 107 y 108 del tratado, para lo que se realizan ajustes a los requisitos de los beneficiarios referidos al domicilio fiscal. Finalmente, se modifica la estructura de la Orden CNU 161/2025, de 7 de febrero, dividiéndola en 3 capítulos, por razones de sistemática: el primero recoge el objeto y finalidad de las ayudas, el segundo se refiere a las características y procedimientos aplicables de las ayudas en forma de subvención y el tercero, a las características y procedimiento aplicable a los premios. El proyecto se adecúa a los principios de buena regulación contenidos en el artículo 129 de la Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, del Procedimiento Administrativo Común de las Administraciones Públicas. Es proporcional ya que contiene la regulación mínima que exige la normativa sobre ayudas y subvenciones e impone las obligaciones necesarias mínimas de acuerdo con dicha normativa para atender a las necesidades expuestas. Garantiza el principio de seguridad jurídica, ya que es coherente con el resto del ordenamiento jurídico, nacional y europeo, y genera un marco normativo integrado, claro y de certidumbre, que facilita su conocimiento y comprensión y, por lo tanto, la actuación y toma de decisiones de las personas y empresas. evaluation.eligibility_reason: Kalfrisa es empresa con personalidad jurídica propia, domiciliada en España (Zaragoza, Aragón), no está excluida por tipo de entidad ni circunstancias del artículo 13 de la Ley 38/2003. Sin embargo, Aragón no figura en la lista de Comunidades Autónomas elegibles (Andalucía, Illes Balears, Canarias, Castilla y León, Castilla-La Mancha, Comunidad Valenciana, Extremadura, Galicia, Región de Murcia). La convocatoria exige que la disponibilidad de fondos FEDER en todas las Comunidades Autónomas en las que se ubique el proyecto sea un requisito para obtener financiación. Kalfrisa, con sede en Aragón, no cumple este requisito territorial.
positive_evidence: Kalfrisa posee capacidades en tecnologías limpias y eficientes (recuperación de calor residual, electrificación térmica, combustión de bajas emisiones, tratamiento de emisiones) alineadas con el eje 'Tecnologías limpias y eficientes en el uso de recursos' de la convocatoria.
Experiencia demostrada en proyectos I+D de cooperación (HIGH2-FURNACES, DESCARB-e, EDPIC, LIFE ABATE, e-RTO, RAFeRTO, DT4RAF, IGNITE) que evidencia capacidad de trabajo en consorcio.
Perfil de empresa industrial con TRL preferente 4-7 compatible con investigación relevante basada en tecnologías disruptivas.
Presupuesto total de 138 millones de euros y múltiples líneas regionales ofrecen potencial de financiación significativa si se resuelve la barrera geográfica.
risks_and_unknowns: Barrera crítica: Kalfrisa tiene sede en Aragón, que no está incluida en la lista de Comunidades Autónomas elegibles. La convocatoria exige disponibilidad de fondos FEDER en todas las Comunidades en las que se ubique el proyecto. Esto hace que Kalfrisa sea inelegible como beneficiaria con sede en Aragón, a menos que participe en un consorcio liderado desde una región elegible y el proyecto no requiera fondos FEDER en Aragón.
Consorcio obligatorio: la convocatoria requiere proyectos de I+D en cooperación liderados por empresas. Kalfrisa podría participar como socio industrial, pero no como líder si su sede es Aragón.
Falta de especificación de TRL mínimo y máximo: no consta rango de TRL aceptado, lo que impide validar si TRL 4-7 de Kalfrisa es compatible.

Falta de especificación de CNAE elegibles: no consta restricción por sector CNAE. Kalfrisa declara CNAE 2899 (fabricación de maquinaria no clasificada en otra parte) y 7112 (ingeniería y otras actividades relacionadas). Sin restricción explícita, se asume elegibilidad sectorial, pero debe verificarse.
Falta de presupuesto mínimo y máximo de proyecto: no consta coste mínimo ni máximo de proyecto, ni tasa de cofinanciación. Impide estimar viabilidad presupuestaria.
Falta de acciones elegibles específicas: el campo 'eligible_actions' está vacío. No consta qué tipos de actividades (I+D, demostración, piloto, etc.) financia la convocatoria.
Falta de detalles sobre gastos elegibles e ineligibles: la convocatoria no especifica qué gastos son elegibles (personal, equipamiento, subcontratación, etc.) ni cuáles se excluyen.
Plazo de apertura: la convocatoria abre el 1 de octubre de 2026 (fecha de referencia: 20 de agosto de 2026). Faltan 41 días para la apertura; no hay certeza de que se publique conforme a lo previsto.
Falta de información sobre rol recomendado: sin detalles sobre acciones y presupuesto, no es posible determinar si Kalfrisa actuaría como líder tecnológico, demostrador, proveedor o socio industrial.
partner_needs: Socio líder empresarial ubicado en una de las Comunidades Autónomas elegibles (preferentemente Galicia, Castilla-La Mancha o Andalucía, que concentran 51, 19 y 18 millones de euros respectivamente).
Organismos de investigación, universidades o centros tecnológicos en la región elegida para fortalecer el consorcio y cumplir requisito de cooperación público-privada.
Potencial socio industrial complementario en la región elegida si el proyecto requiere demostración en instalación de tercero.

Sin embargo, su sede en Aragón —fuera de la lista de Comunidades Autónomas elegibles— la hace inelegible como beneficiaria principal. Podría participar como socio industrial en un consorcio liderado desde región elegible, siempre que el proyecto no requiera fondos FEDER en Aragón. Faltan datos críticos: TRL mínimo/máximo, CNAE restringidos, acciones elegibles, gastos, tasa de cofinanciación y presupuesto de proyecto. La convocatoria abre el 1 de octubre de 2026 (plazo: 41 días desde referencia). Requiere consorcio obligatorio. Recomendación: esperar apertura oficial, verificar si se admiten socios sin fondos FEDER en región no elegible, e identificar líder empresarial en región elegida.

Contactar con potenciales líderes empresariales en Galicia, Castilla-La Mancha o Andalucía para explorar liderazgo conjunto. Verificar en bases si se permite participación de socios sin asignación de fondos FEDER en regiones no elegibles. Confirmar TRL, acciones elegibles y presupuesto una vez publicadas las bases.

raw_document.description: Financiación de proyectos bilaterales de I+D en cooperación con socios internacionales, con certificación y seguimiento unilateral CDTI. Convocatoria permanente durante todo 2026 con dos fechas de corte. Instrumento para proyectos de combustión industrial y eficiencia térmica con partners europeos.

evidence: Convocatoria permanente durante todo 2026 con dos fechas de corte
Instrumento para proyectos de combustión industrial y eficiencia térmica con partners europeos

evaluation.eligibility_reason: Convocatoria permanente CDTI sin especificación de tipos de entidad elegibles, geografías, presupuestos, TRL ni requisitos de consorcio detallados en los hechos extraídos. Kalfrisa como empresa mediana española con CNAE 2899 (fabricación de maquinaria) es potencialmente elegible, pero requiere verificación contra bases de regulación CDTI no incluidas en la fuente. Consortium_required=true confirma obligatoriedad de socio internacional, que Kalfrisa no posee en los datos proporcionados.
positive_evidence: Kalfrisa posee experiencia demostrada en combustión industrial, recuperación de calor residual y eficiencia térmica (HIGH2-FURNACES, DESCARB-e, LIFE ABATE, e-RTO, RAFeRTO)
Convocatoria permanente abierta hasta 2026-12-31 con dos fechas de corte, sin presión de cierre inmediato
Instrumento explícitamente orientado a proyectos de combustión industrial y eficiencia térmica con partners europeos, alineado con capacidades core de Kalfrisa
Ayuda parcialmente reembolsable compatible con modelo de demostración industrial de Kalfrisa
Kalfrisa ubicada en Aragón, región con ecosistema de investigación disponible (CIRCE, Universidad de Zaragoza I3A/LIFEn, CLENAR)
risks_and_unknowns: Ausencia de presupuesto total, máximo de ayuda, cofinanciación mínima y rango de coste de proyecto: imposible evaluar viabilidad financiera
Ausencia de rango TRL: no se confirma si la línea acepta TRL 4-7 (preferente en Kalfrisa) o requiere TRL superiores
Consortium_required=true sin identificación de socio internacional: Kalfrisa debe identificar y comprometer partner europeo antes de solicitar
Ausencia de temas/acciones elegibles específicas: no consta si la línea cubre recuperación de calor, hibridación H2, electrificación térmica u otras áreas de Kalfrisa
Naturaleza de «ayuda parcialmente reembolsable» no especificada: desconocido si es préstamo, subvención con reembolso condicionado u otro mecanismo
Falta de evidencia sobre elegibilidad geográfica del socio internacional (¿UE27, EEE, asociados Horizon?)
Rol de Kalfrisa no explícito: podría ser líder del proyecto, socio tecnológico o demostrador, con implicaciones diferentes en elegibilidad y presupuesto
partner_needs: Socio internacional europeo con capacidad en sistemas energéticos, análisis de ciclo de vida o modelización térmica para cumplir requisito de bilateralidad

Preferentemente: CIRCE (Aragón, energy_systems + lca), Universidad de Zaragoza I3A/LIFEn (Aragón, lca) o CENER/CIEMAT (España, energy_systems + lca) como socios españoles; requiere identificación de socio extranjero
Socio con experiencia en proyectos CDTI o Horizon Europe para navegación administrativa
evaluation.resumen: Kalfrisa encaja tecnológicamente en línea CDTI de combustión industrial y eficiencia térmica: experiencia en recuperación de calor, hornos de bajas emisiones, hibridación H2 y gemelos digitales alinea con objeto de convocatoria. evaluation.eligibility_reason: La convocatoria CDTI PID no especifica tipos de entidad elegibles, CNAE admisibles ni geografías restringidas en los hechos extraídos. Kalfrisa (CNAE 2899, empresa mediana, Zaragoza) encaja potencialmente en modalidad individual (sin consorcio obligatorio) y en acciones de I+D industrial y desarrollo experimental. (2) si CNAE 2899 (fabricación de máquinas y equipos) es explícitamente elegible; (3) estado actual de la ventanilla abierta y plazo de presentación vigente.
positive_evidence: Kalfrisa posee capacidades en recuperación de calor residual, hornos industriales, combustión con hidrógeno (hasta 100% H2) y electrificación de procesos térmicos, alineadas con etiquetas hydrogen_combustion y energy_efficiency de la convocatoria.
Experiencia demostrada en proyectos I+D (HIGH2-FURNACES, DESCARB-e, EDPIC, LIFE ABATE, e-RTO, RAFeRTO, DT4RAF, IGNITE) con TRL 4-7 y demostraciones industriales.
Modalidad individual (sin consorcio obligatorio) permite a Kalfrisa actuar como solicitante único si el presupuesto mínimo (175.000 €) se alcanza.
Acciones elegibles (investigación industrial, desarrollo experimental, mejora de procesos y productos) coinciden con el portafolio de I+D de Kalfrisa.
Tasa de financiación del 85% con componente no reembolsable (10-33%) es atractiva para proyectos de demostración industrial.
risks_and_unknowns: Estado de la convocatoria marcado como 'unknown' en los hechos; aunque se indica 'ventanilla abierta' y 'deterministic_call_status: open', no constan fecha de apertura, plazo de cierre ni confirmación de vigencia a 2026-08-20.
No se especifican tipos de entidad elegibles ni CNAE admisibles; no puede confirmarse que CNAE 2899 sea explícitamente aceptado.
Presupuesto mínimo de 175.000 € es conocido, pero no constan máximos ni distribución de costes elegibles (personal, equipos, subcontratación, etc.).
TRL mínimo y máximo no especificados; aunque Kalfrisa opera preferentemente en TRL 4-7, no se confirma si la línea acepta este rango.

Modalidad individual viable, pero si Kalfrisa requiere socios (p. ej., para validación, certificación o escalado), la modalidad de cooperación nacional (consorcio obligatorio) sería alternativa; ambas comparten condiciones base.
Geografía: no consta restricción a España, pero CDTI es financiador nacional; se asume elegibilidad de beneficiarios españoles sin confirmación explícita.
partner_needs: Validación de seguridad y rendimiento en combustión con hidrógeno: CIDAUT (combustion, hydrogen_combustion) o Fundación Hidrógeno Aragón (hydrogen_safety, hydrogen_supply).
Análisis de ciclo de vida (LCA) y sistemas energéticos: CIRCE, CENER o CIEMAT (energy_systems, lca).
Investigación en combustión y caracterización de mezclas H2: Universidad de Zaragoza — I3A/LIFEn (hydrogen_combustion, lca).
Si el proyecto incluye recuperación de calor y eficiencia energética, socios con expertise en sistemas energéticos (CIRCE, CENER, CIEMAT) reforzarían la propuesta.
evaluation.resumen: Kalfrisa encaja en la línea PID modalidad individual (sin consorcio obligatorio) por sus capacidades en I+D industrial de procesos térmicos, combustión con hidrógeno y recuperación de calor, alineadas con las acciones y etiquetas de la convocatoria. El presupuesto mínimo (175.000 €) es accesible para un proyecto de demostración o escalado de tecnología propia. (2) aceptación explícita de CNAE 2899; (3) estado vigente de la ventanilla abierta y plazo de presentación a fecha 2026-08-20; (4) TRL mínimo y máximo aceptados; (5) detalles de gastos elegibles y máximos de subvención.
evaluation.accion: Verificar inmediatamente: (a) estado y plazo vigente de la convocatoria CDTI PID a 2026-08-20; de empresa y CNAE en las bases; (c) TRL mínimo/máximo y detalles de elegibilidad de gastos. Si se confirma elegibilidad, preparar propuesta en modalidad individual enfocada en demostración industrial de combustión con hidrógeno o recuperación de calor residual (TRL 5-7). Considerar incorporación de socios (CIDAUT, FHA, CIRCE, CIEMAT, UnizarI3A) en modalidad cooperación nacional si se requiere validación externa o análisis LCA.
